business.title: A consistency-oriented adaptive power allocation method for battery energy storage systems under seasonal wind-photovoltaic scenarios
business.desc: With the continuous increase in wind and photovoltaic penetration, battery energy storage systems (BESSs) have become an important supporting resource for power balancing and flexible regulation in renewable energy stations. However, during the long-term operation of multi-cluster parallel battery systems, state-of-charge (SOC) inconsistency continuously accumulates owing to inter-cluster capacity differences, deviations in initial states, and operational nonuniformity. This accumulation further leads to unbalanced cluster responses, premature triggering of boundary constraints, and a reduction in the available regulation capability of the system. To address these issues, this study proposes a consistency-oriented adaptive optimal power allocation (COAO) method for seasonal wind–photovoltaic operating scenarios. First, daily operating feature vectors are constructed from annual wind power, photovoltaic, and load data, and fuzzy C-means clustering is employed to extract four typical operating scenarios corresponding to spring, summer, autumn, and winter, thereby establishing a unified cross-season evaluation framework. Second, for multi-cluster electrochemical energy storage systems, a consistency-oriented mathematical model is developed that incorporates cluster-level SOC dynamics, SOC safety boundaries, power constraints, ramp-rate constraints, and a directional exit mechanism. Furthermore, a cluster-level priority scoring function is constructed by comprehensively considering direction-related SOC margins and capacity differences, and adaptive weight adjustment together with feasible-region optimization correction is introduced based on consistency indicators. In this way, both power execution capability and consistency maintenance capability can be achieved under engineering constraints. Finally, under the four seasonal representative scenarios, the proposed method is systematically compared with three benchmark allocation strategies, namely state-of-charge proportional allocation (SCPA), maximum residual power-based ranked water-filling (MRWF), and model-predictive-control-based SOC balancing (MPC-SOC), over 30 paired simulations. The results show that COAO consistently achieves the lowest mean SOC range and SOC standard deviation and also provides the best overall power-tracking performance across all four seasonal scenarios. This study can provide methodological support for the refined operational control of multi-cluster energy storage systems in renewable energy stations.

business.title: Microsecond-pulsed nanocalorimetry: a scalable approach for ultrasensitive heat capacity measurements
business.desc: We introduce a nanocalorimetric technique based on microsecond-pulsed heating (µs-PHnC) that enables high-sensitivity, quasi-isothermal heat capacity measurements on nanoscale samples. Such resolution is critical for exploring thermodynamic signatures in low-dimensional materials, where conventional techniques fall short. By confining thermal excitation to microsecond timescales, this approach minimizes lateral heat diffusion, reduces heat capacity addenda to below 10⁻⁹ J K-1, and achieves noise densities as low as 75 pJ K⁻¹ √Hz mm⁻², unlocking precise thermodynamic characterization of subnanogram samples in areas as small as 30 × 30 µm². The method delivers exceptional temperature homogeneity, as demonstrated by resolving sharp phase transitions, such as the antiferromagnetic transition in ultrathin CoO films, with unprecedented clarity. Its quasi-static operation is inherently compatible with external stimuli, including magnetic and electric fields, thereby expanding its utility for in-operando thermodynamic studies. The method is scalable in lateral dimension because the microsecond excitation window confines the thermal diffusion length, allowing the effective calorimetric volume to shrink with the device footprint. This advancement establishes a robust and scalable platform for probing thermal phenomena in nanostructured and low-dimensional materials, significantly broadening the scope of nanocalorimetry.
